effective_report.review_summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.
scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. Their liquefaction and fermentation tanks, jet cooker, cooking column, enzyme calculations, prices, and cost lines are not merged into this study’s equipment register.

“Energy calculation” has bioethanol project headers and no populated stream or energy data in the supplied cells. Do not merge its stream numbers with the active balance; repeated stream numbers do not establish identity.

The active balance names Anaerobic Digestion as the destination for settled biomass (AS26), but provides no digestion unit identity or relationship to an installed digestion plant. Keep digestion outside the equipment register pending scope confirmation.

This region describes wheat milling, slurry preparation, cooking/liquefaction, cooling, yeast addition, fermentation, CO2 to CCS, and fermented mash to distillation. The primary equipment register instead identifies wastewater-treatment units; no relationship connects the two process scopes, so do not merge them or add ethanol-process equipment to that register.
Stream numbers 1–18 in Energy calculation are local to that sheet and are distinct from identically numbered streams on Mass and Energy Balance.

Most component and total flow entries are #REF!, not usable measured values. The worksheet also labels energy columns kJ/hr while Python interpreted these as unresolved component/total flow; they represent energy terms, not mass-flow evidence.

The energy calculation includes component heat-capacity entries (HC) and temperature changes, but does not provide enough valid inputs to establish numerical heat duties. Do not infer missing quantities from the process narrative.

engineering_review.summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.

analysis_schedule.rationale: FlowValue editable planning example: fixed capital 30/50/20 across project years 1–3 when two pre-operation construction years are selected; start-up capital and working capital at first operation. Other construction durations use equal capital shares. These percentages are not prescribed by Garrett. Scheduled operation defaults to 100%; no first-year uptake or production ramp is predicted. Different annual percentages require an explicit user scenario; operating hours remain a separate assumption.

report.review_summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.
scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. Their liquefaction and fermentation tanks, jet cooker, cooking column, enzyme calculations, prices, and cost lines are not merged into this study’s equipment register.

“Energy calculation” has bioethanol project headers and no populated stream or energy data in the supplied cells. Do not merge its stream numbers with the active balance; repeated stream numbers do not establish identity.

The active balance names Anaerobic Digestion as the destination for settled biomass (AS26), but provides no digestion unit identity or relationship to an installed digestion plant. Keep digestion outside the equipment register pending scope confirmation.

This region describes wheat milling, slurry preparation, cooking/liquefaction, cooling, yeast addition, fermentation, CO2 to CCS, and fermented mash to distillation. The primary equipment register instead identifies wastewater-treatment units; no relationship connects the two process scopes, so do not merge them or add ethanol-process equipment to that register.
Stream numbers 1–18 in Energy calculation are local to that sheet and are distinct from identically numbered streams on Mass and Energy Balance.

Most component and total flow entries are #REF!, not usable measured values. The worksheet also labels energy columns kJ/hr while Python interpreted these as unresolved component/total flow; they represent energy terms, not mass-flow evidence.

The energy calculation includes component heat-capacity entries (HC) and temperature changes, but does not provide enough valid inputs to establish numerical heat duties. Do not infer missing quantities from the process narrative.

effective_report.review_summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.
scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. Their liquefaction and fermentation tanks, jet cooker, cooking column, enzyme calculations, prices, and cost lines are not merged into this study’s equipment register.

“Energy calculation” has bioethanol project headers and no populated stream or energy data in the supplied cells. Do not merge its stream numbers with the active balance; repeated stream numbers do not establish identity.

The active balance names Anaerobic Digestion as the destination for settled biomass (AS26), but provides no digestion unit identity or relationship to an installed digestion plant. Keep digestion outside the equipment register pending scope confirmation.

This region describes wheat milling, slurry preparation, cooking/liquefaction, cooling, yeast addition, fermentation, CO2 to CCS, and fermented mash to distillation. The primary equipment register instead identifies wastewater-treatment units; no relationship connects the two process scopes, so do not merge them or add ethanol-process equipment to that register.
Stream numbers 1–18 in Energy calculation are local to that sheet and are distinct from identically numbered streams on Mass and Energy Balance.

Most component and total flow entries are #REF!, not usable measured values. The worksheet also labels energy columns kJ/hr while Python interpreted these as unresolved component/total flow; they represent energy terms, not mass-flow evidence.

The energy calculation includes component heat-capacity entries (HC) and temperature changes, but does not provide enough valid inputs to establish numerical heat duties. Do not infer missing quantities from the process narrative.

engineering_review.summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.

analysis_schedule.rationale: FlowValue editable planning example: fixed capital 30/50/20 across project years 1–3 when two pre-operation construction years are selected; start-up capital and working capital at first operation. Other construction durations use equal capital shares. These percentages are not prescribed by Garrett. Scheduled operation defaults to 100%; no first-year uptake or production ramp is predicted. Different annual percentages require an explicit user scenario; operating hours remain a separate assumption.

production_allocation_fraction.limitations: No plant-wide allocation or number of parallel reactors is given.

volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.limitations: Actual biofilm kinetics, substrate loading, oxygen transfer, media area and conversion are unknown; this is not a verified design productivity.
volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.name: volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h
volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.rationale: Explicit preliminary biomass productivity scenario for a fungal biofilm wastewater reactor; no workbook productivity parameter fits this service. working_fraction.limitations: Actual liquid level, gas disengagement and internals determine the usable fraction.
working_fraction.name: working_fraction
working_fraction.rationale: Preliminary usable-volume fraction for a continuous biological reactor vessel.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: Use the directly reported total stream mass flow (v93, kg/h) with the vessel_volume recipe; derive density from mass and volume flow of the same linked stream (v93 and v92) rather than assume a density. The supplied vertical-cylinder OpenPyTEA model is the compatible candidate whose stated capacity range covers the resulting preliminary scenario; the ambiguous workbook tank-volume entries are not assigned to T-003. This is an explicitly assumed storage-inventory scenario, not a measured tank capacity.

sizing.rationale: Use the directly reported total stream mass flow (v93, kg/h) with the vessel_volume recipe; derive density from mass and volume flow of the same linked stream (v93 and v92) rather than assume a density. The sizing relationship is V = (mass flow / density) × residence time / working fraction. The supplied vertical-cylinder OpenPyTEA model is the compatible candidate whose stated capacity range covers the resulting preliminary scenario; the ambiguous workbook tank-volume entries are not assigned to T-003. This is an explicitly assumed storage-inventory scenario, not a measured tank capacity.

Workbook tank-volume entries conflict, so none is selected as T-001 capacity; workbook-wide process times do not establish storage duration. The OpenPyTEA cone-roof tank is a provisional storage configuration and is preferred over the Garrett option. The assumed small scenario may be below the correlation's minimum; retain the physically sized coordinate and disclose the model floor rather than increasing the tank size to fit.

Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

sizing.rationale: T-002 is identified as a sucrose storage tank. Use the linked total mass flow v71 with an explicit solution-density estimate; the sizing relationship is mass flow ÷ density × assumed inventory duration ÷ working fraction. v70 is the corresponding volumetric-flow context but is not the selected recipe input. The conflicting workbook volume entries cannot be attributed reliably to T-002, and workbook-wide process times are not storage duration. The OpenPyTEA vertical-cylinder correlation has a capacity domain that covers a plausible small storage scenario and is preferred to Garrett; no size is altered to match a curve.

report.review_summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.
scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. Their liquefaction and fermentation tanks, jet cooker, cooking column, enzyme calculations, prices, and cost lines are not merged into this study’s equipment register.

“Energy calculation” has bioethanol project headers and no populated stream or energy data in the supplied cells. Do not merge its stream numbers with the active balance; repeated stream numbers do not establish identity.

The active balance names Anaerobic Digestion as the destination for settled biomass (AS26), but provides no digestion unit identity or relationship to an installed digestion plant. Keep digestion outside the equipment register pending scope confirmation.

This region describes wheat milling, slurry preparation, cooking/liquefaction, cooling, yeast addition, fermentation, CO2 to CCS, and fermented mash to distillation. The primary equipment register instead identifies wastewater-treatment units; no relationship connects the two process scopes, so do not merge them or add ethanol-process equipment to that register.
Stream numbers 1–18 in Energy calculation are local to that sheet and are distinct from identically numbered streams on Mass and Energy Balance.

Most component and total flow entries are #REF!, not usable measured values. The worksheet also labels energy columns kJ/hr while Python interpreted these as unresolved component/total flow; they represent energy terms, not mass-flow evidence.

The energy calculation includes component heat-capacity entries (HC) and temperature changes, but does not provide enough valid inputs to establish numerical heat duties. Do not infer missing quantities from the process narrative.

report.review_summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.
scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. Their liquefaction and fermentation tanks, jet cooker, cooking column, enzyme calculations, prices, and cost lines are not merged into this study’s equipment register.

“Energy calculation” has bioethanol project headers and no populated stream or energy data in the supplied cells. Do not merge its stream numbers with the active balance; repeated stream numbers do not establish identity.

The active balance names Anaerobic Digestion as the destination for settled biomass (AS26), but provides no digestion unit identity or relationship to an installed digestion plant. Keep digestion outside the equipment register pending scope confirmation.

This region describes wheat milling, slurry preparation, cooking/liquefaction, cooling, yeast addition, fermentation, CO2 to CCS, and fermented mash to distillation. The primary equipment register instead identifies wastewater-treatment units; no relationship connects the two process scopes, so do not merge them or add ethanol-process equipment to that register.
Stream numbers 1–18 in Energy calculation are local to that sheet and are distinct from identically numbered streams on Mass and Energy Balance.

Most component and total flow entries are #REF!, not usable measured values. The worksheet also labels energy columns kJ/hr while Python interpreted these as unresolved component/total flow; they represent energy terms, not mass-flow evidence.

The energy calculation includes component heat-capacity entries (HC) and temperature changes, but does not provide enough valid inputs to establish numerical heat duties. Do not infer missing quantities from the process narrative.

Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

sizing.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

The steel clarifier OpenPyTEA model is preferred among compatible candidates; its published area domain is 80–8000 ft2, while the selected loading scenario gives an area expected to fall within that domain. This is a provisional configuration, not evidence that mechanical equipment or steel construction was specified or verified.

sizing.rationale: The linked stream is the sulfuric-acid supplier feed to T-001; use its total volumetric flow (v7), not its mass flow, because it directly matches the volume-flow basis. The sizing relationship is inlet volume flow × assumed inventory duration ÷ working fraction. Workbook tank-volume entries conflict, so none is selected as T-001 capacity; workbook-wide process times do not establish storage duration. The OpenPyTEA cone-roof tank is a provisional storage configuration and is preferred over the Garrett option. The assumed small scenario may be below the correlation's minimum; retain the physically sized coordinate and disclose the model floor rather than increasing the tank size to fit.

input_resolution.rationale: Use the linked wastewater stream’s reported volumetric flow, v44 (125.1275 m³/h), as the liquid duty-flow coordinate and convert units directly to the model’s US_MGD coordinate. input_resolution.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. sizing.rationale: Use the directly reported total stream mass flow (v93, kg/h) with the vessel_volume recipe; derive density from mass and volume flow of the same linked stream (v93 and v92) rather than assume a density. The sizing relationship is V = (mass flow / density) × residence time / working fraction. The supplied vertical-cylinder OpenPyTEA model is the compatible candidate whose stated capacity range covers the resulting preliminary scenario; the ambiguous workbook tank-volume entries are not assigned to T-003. This is an explicitly assumed storage-inventory scenario, not a measured tank capacity.

effective_report.review_summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.
scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. Their liquefaction and fermentation tanks, jet cooker, cooking column, enzyme calculations, prices, and cost lines are not merged into this study’s equipment register.

“Energy calculation” has bioethanol project headers and no populated stream or energy data in the supplied cells. Do not merge its stream numbers with the active balance; repeated stream numbers do not establish identity.

The active balance names Anaerobic Digestion as the destination for settled biomass (AS26), but provides no digestion unit identity or relationship to an installed digestion plant. Keep digestion outside the equipment register pending scope confirmation.

This region describes wheat milling, slurry preparation, cooking/liquefaction, cooling, yeast addition, fermentation, CO2 to CCS, and fermented mash to distillation. The primary equipment register instead identifies wastewater-treatment units; no relationship connects the two process scopes, so do not merge them or add ethanol-process equipment to that register.
Stream numbers 1–18 in Energy calculation are local to that sheet and are distinct from identically numbered streams on Mass and Energy Balance.

Most component and total flow entries are #REF!, not usable measured values. The worksheet also labels energy columns kJ/hr while Python interpreted these as unresolved component/total flow; they represent energy terms, not mass-flow evidence.

The energy calculation includes component heat-capacity entries (HC) and temperature changes, but does not provide enough valid inputs to establish numerical heat duties. Do not infer missing quantities from the process narrative.

reasoning: Fluid handling and chemical feeds raise scope; limited listed equipment and no stated recycle or heat-exchange network temper it.
Pumping and bioreactor services require wiring; no motor list, electrical loads or upstream supply scope is given.
pH and bioreactor control imply meaningful automation, but control philosophy and instrumentation detail are absent.
Sterile air and wastewater handling need services; utility generation and shared offsite provision are unspecified.
Tanks and process vessels need supports; equipment sizes, layout and ground conditions are unknown.
No heated process duty is evident in the quantified wastewater train; temperature requirements remain unconfirmed.
Chemical storage merits protective and safety provisions, while the listed process shows no major flammable inventory.
New-plant access and drainage are plausible allowances; site grading and existing infrastructure are unknown.
Wastewater discharge and vented gas warrant monitoring and treatment consideration; discharge limits and permitting scope are absent.
The listed train appears compact and process-led; laboratory, storage and support-building needs are not specified.
Land purchase is not stated; zero is appropriate unless the project acquires a site.
New-plant integration and uncertain scope add engineering effort; the short listed equipment train limits apparent complexity.
A relatively limited listed train suggests modest contracting scope, but execution strategy and package boundaries are unknown.
Conflicting process descriptions and incomplete equipment scope create uncertainty; no site or design maturity data justify an extreme allowance.
Biological process commissioning may need ramp-up; staffing, validation and startup duration are not provided.
Chemical and sucrose inventories imply operating stock; supply terms, inventory policy and operating schedule are unspecified.

scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. Their liquefaction and fermentation tanks, jet cooker, cooking column, enzyme calculations, prices, and cost lines are not merged into this study’s equipment register.

“Energy calculation” has bioethanol project headers and no populated stream or energy data in the supplied cells. Do not merge its stream numbers with the active balance; repeated stream numbers do not establish identity.

The active balance names Anaerobic Digestion as the destination for settled biomass (AS26), but provides no digestion unit identity or relationship to an installed digestion plant. Keep digestion outside the equipment register pending scope confirmation.

This region describes wheat milling, slurry preparation, cooking/liquefaction, cooling, yeast addition, fermentation, CO2 to CCS, and fermented mash to distillation. The primary equipment register instead identifies wastewater-treatment units; no relationship connects the two process scopes, so do not merge them or add ethanol-process equipment to that register.
Stream numbers 1–18 in Energy calculation are local to that sheet and are distinct from identically numbered streams on Mass and Energy Balance.

Most component and total flow entries are #REF!, not usable measured values. The worksheet also labels energy columns kJ/hr while Python interpreted these as unresolved component/total flow; they represent energy terms, not mass-flow evidence.

The energy calculation includes component heat-capacity entries (HC) and temperature changes, but does not provide enough valid inputs to establish numerical heat duties. Do not infer missing quantities from the process narrative.

engineering_review.summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.

Different annual percentages require an explicit user scenario; operating hours remain a separate assumption.

product_rate_kg_h.name: product_rate_kg_h
product_rate_kg_h.rationale: Preliminary product-rate scenario based on the linked treated-effluent biomass component observation v137 (100 kg/h), used only as a scenario basis for this reactor's costing coordinate; it is not evidence that R-001 produces or allocates all of that biomass.

production_allocation_fraction.limitations: No plant-wide allocation or number of parallel reactors is given.
production_allocation_fraction.name: production_allocation_fraction
production_allocation_fraction.rationale: Provisional assumption that this single identified reactor is assigned the scenario's biomass production; editable to reflect parallel units or process allocation.

volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.limitations: Actual biofilm kinetics, substrate loading, oxygen transfer, media area and conversion are unknown; this is not a verified design productivity.
volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.name: volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h
volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.rationale: Explicit preliminary biomass productivity scenario for a fungal biofilm wastewater reactor; no workbook productivity parameter fits this service. Chosen to yield a screening vessel-core coordinate within the supplied fermenter correlation's stated domain, not to assert measured kinetics.

working_fraction.limitations: Actual liquid level, gas disengagement and internals determine the usable fraction.
working_fraction.name: working_fraction
working_fraction.rationale: Preliminary usable-volume fraction for a continuous biological reactor vessel.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

equation.scope: Explicit preliminary production/productivity scenario; no workbook flow or connection is created. Does not validate biological kinetics, mass transfer, residence time, capacity or complete bioreactor package scope.

product_rate_kg_h.limitations: Downstream biomass measurement does not establish reactor yield, production rate, or attribution to R-001; verify process mass balance and unit allocation.
product_rate_kg_h.name: product_rate_kg_h
product_rate_kg_h.rationale: Preliminary product-rate scenario based on the linked treated-effluent biomass component observation v137 (100 kg/h), used only as a scenario basis for this reactor's costing coordinate; it is not evidence that R-001 produces or allocates all of that biomass.

production_allocation_fraction.limitations: No plant-wide allocation or number of parallel reactors is given.
production_allocation_fraction.name: production_allocation_fraction
production_allocation_fraction.rationale: Provisional assumption that this single identified reactor is assigned the scenario's biomass production; editable to reflect parallel units or process allocation.

volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.limitations: Actual biofilm kinetics, substrate loading, oxygen transfer, media area and conversion are unknown; this is not a verified design productivity.
volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.name: volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h
volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.rationale: Explicit preliminary biomass productivity scenario for a fungal biofilm wastewater reactor; no workbook productivity parameter fits this service. Chosen to yield a screening vessel-core coordinate within the supplied fermenter correlation's stated domain, not to assert measured kinetics.

working_fraction.limitations: Actual liquid level, gas disengagement and internals determine the usable fraction.
working_fraction.name: working_fraction
working_fraction.rationale: Preliminary usable-volume fraction for a continuous biological reactor vessel.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: The explicit service name identifies a treated-wastewater biomass settler. For a preliminary mechanically equipped clarifier configuration, use the linked liquid flow measurement v138 (125.88489 m3/h) and the clarifier-area relationship A = Q / surface overflow rate. The steel clarifier OpenPyTEA model is preferred among compatible candidates; its published area domain is 80–8000 ft2, while the selected loading scenario gives an area expected to fall within that domain. This is a provisional configuration, not evidence that mechanical equipment or steel construction was specified or verified.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: The linked stream is the sulfuric-acid supplier feed to T-001; use its total volumetric flow (v7), not its mass flow, because it directly matches the volume-flow basis. The sizing relationship is inlet volume flow × assumed inventory duration ÷ working fraction. Workbook tank-volume entries conflict, so none is selected as T-001 capacity; workbook-wide process times do not establish storage duration. The OpenPyTEA cone-roof tank is a provisional storage configuration and is preferred over the Garrett option. The assumed small scenario may be below the correlation's minimum; retain the physically sized coordinate and disclose the model floor rather than increasing the tank size to fit.

report.review_summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.
scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. Their liquefaction and fermentation tanks, jet cooker, cooking column, enzyme calculations, prices, and cost lines are not merged into this study’s equipment register.

“Energy calculation” has bioethanol project headers and no populated stream or energy data in the supplied cells. Do not merge its stream numbers with the active balance; repeated stream numbers do not establish identity.

The active balance names Anaerobic Digestion as the destination for settled biomass (AS26), but provides no digestion unit identity or relationship to an installed digestion plant. Keep digestion outside the equipment register pending scope confirmation.

This region describes wheat milling, slurry preparation, cooking/liquefaction, cooling, yeast addition, fermentation, CO2 to CCS, and fermented mash to distillation. The primary equipment register instead identifies wastewater-treatment units; no relationship connects the two process scopes, so do not merge them or add ethanol-process equipment to that register.
Stream numbers 1–18 in Energy calculation are local to that sheet and are distinct from identically numbered streams on Mass and Energy Balance.

Most component and total flow entries are #REF!, not usable measured values. The worksheet also labels energy columns kJ/hr while Python interpreted these as unresolved component/total flow; they represent energy terms, not mass-flow evidence.

The energy calculation includes component heat-capacity entries (HC) and temperature changes, but does not provide enough valid inputs to establish numerical heat duties. Do not infer missing quantities from the process narrative.

report.review_summary:
The active process basis is the fungal biofilm lignin-removal balance on “Mass and Energy Balance.” Add its omitted equipment and missing stream observations, and retain the downstream anaerobic digestion reference as a product destination, not installed equipment. The other supplied sheets describe a separate bioethanol project and are not evidence for equipment in the active process.
The Energy calculation sheet is an ethanol-from-wheat energy-balance region, not evidence for additional equipment in the wastewater-treatment train registered on Mass and Energy Balance. Its mass-flow and heat-duty cells are largely #REF!, so the stream descriptions and process sequence are recoverable but useful numerical balances are not. Repeated stream numbers across sheets are not treated as shared stream identities.
scope_notes: “Unit op quantity and sizing,” “Enzyme Calcs,” and “CAPEX - Liquefaction” identify a Production Capacity Increase / Bioethanol Plant, unlike the active lignin-removal balance. Their liquefaction and fermentation tanks, jet cooker, cooking column, enzyme calculations, prices, and cost lines are not merged into this study’s equipment register.

“Energy calculation” has bioethanol project headers and no populated stream or energy data in the supplied cells. Do not merge its stream numbers with the active balance; repeated stream numbers do not establish identity.

The active balance names Anaerobic Digestion as the destination for settled biomass (AS26), but provides no digestion unit identity or relationship to an installed digestion plant. Keep digestion outside the equipment register pending scope confirmation.

This region describes wheat milling, slurry preparation, cooking/liquefaction, cooling, yeast addition, fermentation, CO2 to CCS, and fermented mash to distillation. The primary equipment register instead identifies wastewater-treatment units; no relationship connects the two process scopes, so do not merge them or add ethanol-process equipment to that register.
Stream numbers 1–18 in Energy calculation are local to that sheet and are distinct from identically numbered streams on Mass and Energy Balance.

Most component and total flow entries are #REF!, not usable measured values. The worksheet also labels energy columns kJ/hr while Python interpreted these as unresolved component/total flow; they represent energy terms, not mass-flow evidence.

The energy calculation includes component heat-capacity entries (HC) and temperature changes, but does not provide enough valid inputs to establish numerical heat duties. Do not infer missing quantities from the process narrative.

Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

This is a provisional configuration, not evidence that mechanical equipment or steel construction was specified or verified.

production_allocation_fraction.limitations: No plant-wide allocation or number of parallel reactors is given.
production_allocation_fraction.name: production_allocation_fraction
production_allocation_fraction.rationale: Provisional assumption that this single identified reactor is assigned the scenario's biomass production; editable to reflect parallel units or process allocation.

volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.limitations: Actual biofilm kinetics, substrate loading, oxygen transfer, media area and conversion are unknown; this is not a verified design productivity.
volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.name: volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h
volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.rationale: Explicit preliminary biomass productivity scenario for a fungal biofilm wastewater reactor; no workbook productivity parameter fits this service. Chosen to yield a screening vessel-core coordinate within the supplied fermenter correlation's stated domain, not to assert measured kinetics.

working_fraction.limitations: Actual liquid level, gas disengagement and internals determine the usable fraction.
working_fraction.name: working_fraction
working_fraction.rationale: Preliminary usable-volume fraction for a continuous biological reactor vessel.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

production_allocation_fraction.limitations: No plant-wide allocation or number of parallel reactors is given.

volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.limitations: Actual biofilm kinetics, substrate loading, oxygen transfer, media area and conversion are unknown; this is not a verified design productivity.
volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h.name: volumetric_productivity_kg_m3_h

working_fraction.limitations: Actual liquid level, gas disengagement and internals determine the usable fraction.
working_fraction.name: working_fraction
working_fraction.rationale: Preliminary usable-volume fraction for a continuous biological reactor vessel.

sizing_evidence.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing_evidence.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: T-002 is identified as a sucrose storage tank. Use the linked total mass flow v71 with an explicit solution-density estimate; the sizing relationship is mass flow ÷ density × assumed inventory duration ÷ working fraction. v70 is the corresponding volumetric-flow context but is not the selected recipe input. The conflicting workbook volume entries cannot be attributed reliably to T-002, and workbook-wide process times are not storage duration. The OpenPyTEA vertical-cylinder correlation has a capacity domain that covers a plausible small storage scenario and is preferred to Garrett; no size is altered to match a curve.

sizing.notice: User-input sizing scenario, not a validated design. No costing equation or workbook observation changed.
sizing.rationale: R-001 is explicitly a fungal biofilm bioreactor. Use the supplied vessel_productivity route rather than treating an oxygen/reactant gas flow as liquid throughput or claiming a measured per-vessel volume. The scenario uses the available downstream biomass component v137 as a clearly qualified product-rate proxy, with explicit allocation, productivity and working-fraction assumptions; Python calculates volume from those parameters. Continuous operation is a provisional assumption consistent with the linked wastewater feed and treatment service. The workbook's 48 h fermentation time is not specific to this biofilm reactor and is rejected for this sizing basis. Select the supplied OpenPyTEA fermenter model as a vessel-core proxy; do not extrapolate beyond its 35 m3 maximum.
